lines.speaker: Old Barnaby
lines.text: Ah, it's you again! I've been reading about <color=red>prehistoric</color> creatures, though my memory for their names is distinctly unreliable.

lines.speaker: Old Barnaby
lines.text: I've <color=red>composed</color> three riddles on the subject. Solve them all and three new books will be sent to the library.

lines.speaker: Old Barnaby
lines.text: Riddle 1: I was once living bone, but over millions of years minerals replaced me until I became stone. A <color=red>palaeontologist</color> might spend weeks carefully uncovering me. What am I?
lines.hint: Not quite. Which of these began life as bone and slowly turned to stone?
lines.correctText: Correct. A fossil preserves the shape of the original bone in stone.

lines.speaker: Old Barnaby
lines.text: Riddle 2: My name comes from Greek words meaning 'three-horned face', and a bony frill shielded my neck. As a <color=red>herbivore</color>, I'd never have eaten you. What am I?
lines.hint: Not quite. Which name begins with the prefix meaning 'three'?
lines.correctText: Exactly. 'Tri' means three, and 'ceratops' means horned face.

lines.speaker: Old Barnaby
lines.text: Riddle 3: I was a fearsome <color=red>predator</color> with teeth like serrated knives and arms too short to reach my mouth. My name means 'tyrant lizard king'. What am I?
lines.hint: Not quite. Which name contains words that sound like 'tyrant' and 'king'?
lines.correctText: Well reasoned. 'Rex' is Latin for king.

lines.speaker: Old Barnaby
lines.text: Three for three! Your powers of <color=red>deduction</color> are remarkable, and three new volumes are on their way to the library.

afterLines.speaker: Old Barnaby
afterLines.text: I've been <color=red>pondering</color> the fact that birds descended from dinosaurs. Every pigeon in camp may be a very distant cousin of a Tyrannosaurus!
